source: OpenStax A&P 2e: 8.2 Bones of the Upper Limb (and glossary); 8.5; 9.4; 9.5

main.t: The wrist bone at the base of the thumb, first in the second row of carpal bones (trapezium).

simpler.t: The trapezium is the wrist bone at the base of your thumb.

deeper.t: Its saddle joint with the first metacarpal gives humans their opposable thumbs.

facts.t: It is the first bone of the second (distal) row, counting from the thumb side.
The scaphoid is above it. The trapezoid is beside it, towards the little finger.
Below it are the first and second metacarpals.

simpler.t: It sits at the base of your thumb, just above the thumb’s palm bone.

deeper.t: It is one of the four carpal bones the flexor retinaculum attaches to.

items.name: Saddle surface
items.t: Its surface for the first metacarpal is saddle-shaped: concave one way and convex the other.

items.name: Surface for the second metacarpal
items.t: A small surface beside it, for the second metacarpal.

items.name: Surfaces for the scaphoid and trapezoid
items.t: It meets the scaphoid above and the trapezoid beside it.

items.name: Front surface
items.t: With the scaphoid, it anchors the outer end of the flexor retinaculum.

simpler.t: It has a saddle-shaped joint surface for the thumb.

deeper.t: The saddle shape lets the thumb move within the plane of the palm and out in front of it.

facts.t: The saddle joint is biaxial: the thumb can move in two planes.
Opposition, touching the thumb to a fingertip, combines flexion and abduction at this joint.
Its front anchors the flexor retinaculum, which roofs the carpal tunnel.

simpler.t: Its saddle shape lets your thumb swing across to touch your fingertips.

items.name: First carpometacarpal joint
items.t: A saddle joint with the first metacarpal, at the base of the thumb.

items.name: Second metacarpal
items.t: Meets a small surface beside the saddle.

items.name: Trapezoid
items.t: Its neighbour in the second row.

items.name: Flexor retinaculum
items.t: Attached on the thumb side to the trapezium and scaphoid.

simpler.t: It carries the thumb’s palm bone and anchors the roof of the carpal tunnel.

facts.t: It forms by replacing a cartilage model with bone (endochondral ossification), like all limb bones except the clavicle.
Its single ossification centre appears at about the fifth year.
facts.check: Not in OpenStax A&P 2e (chapters 6–9, 12–16, 20). Gray’s 1918 (8.2) gives the fifth year (as the “greater multangular”) (supporting only).

items.injury: An injury to the joint at the base of the thumb.
items.cannotDo: Touch the tip of the thumb to the tip of a finger (opposition).
items.why: Opposition is produced at this joint, by flexion and abduction of the thumb.

items.damaged: The joint between the trapezium and the first metacarpal wears (osteoarthritis).
items.cannotDo: Pinch, open jars or turn keys without pain at the base of the thumb.
items.why: This saddle joint takes the force of every pinch and grip.

items.q: Explain how the trapezium makes the thumb opposable.
model: It forms a saddle joint with the first metacarpal.
A saddle joint is biaxial: the thumb moves in two planes.
The first metacarpal is separate from the others, so it moves freely.
Flexion with abduction at this joint brings the thumb to the fingertips.

items.q: Compare the trapezium and the trapezoid.
model: Both are in the second row, on the thumb side.
The trapezium (“table”) is first; the trapezoid (“resembles a table”) is second.
The trapezium meets the first and second metacarpals; the trapezoid meets only the second.
Only the trapezium anchors the flexor retinaculum.

items.q: Predict which thumb movements are lost if the first carpometacarpal joint is fused.
model: Opposition: touching the thumb to a fingertip.
Flexion and extension of the thumb at this joint.
Abduction and adduction of the thumb.
The joints further along the thumb still bend.

check.stem: What type of joint lies between the trapezium and the first metacarpal?
check.why: The first carpometacarpal joint is a saddle joint.

check.stem: Which bones does the trapezium meet below?
check.why: It meets the first and second metacarpals.

check.stem: Which thumb movement combines flexion and abduction at the first carpometacarpal joint?
check.why: Opposition brings the tip of the thumb to the tip of a finger.
